questions.prompt: The Nyquist criterion determines closed-loop stability by
questions.explanation: The Nyquist plot is \(L(j\omega)\) in the complex plane. The number of encirclements of \(-1\) equals the difference between closed-loop and open-loop RHP poles. Checking \(|L| < 1\) everywhere is too restrictive. \(L = 0\) is not the critical point.

questions.figure_alt: A curve in the complex plane with the critical point marked.

questions.prompt: A stable open-loop system has the Nyquist curve that does not encircle \(-1\). The closed-loop is
questions.explanation: For a stable open-loop (no RHP poles), \(Z = N + P = 0 + 0 = 0\). The closed-loop is stable. If the curve encircles \(-1\) once clockwise, there would be one closed-loop RHP pole.
questions.figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 220" role="img" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12"><title>stable Nyquist</title><line x1="48" y1="104" x2="270" y2="104"/><polygon points="270,104 263.6,106.7 263.6,101.3" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"/><line x1="127.1" y1="180" x2="127.1" y2="28"/><polygon points="127.1,28 129.8,34.4 124.4,34.4" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"/><text x="266" y="118" text-anchor="end" font-size="11" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">Re</text><text x="133.1" y="32" text-anchor="start" font-size="11" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">Im</text><polyline points="254.7,104 190.9,165.3 127.1,134.6 108,104 127.1,73.4 190.9,42.7 254.7,104" stroke-width="2.2"/><circle cx="63.3" cy="104" r="4"/><text x="63.3" y="94" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">−1</text></svg>
questions.figure_alt: A curve in the complex plane with the critical point marked.

questions.prompt: At the gain crossover frequency, \(|L(j\omega_c)| = 1\). On the Nyquist plot, this corresponds to
questions.explanation: The gain crossover is where the magnitude of \(L\) is 1, which is the unit circle on the Nyquist plot. The phase crossover is where the curve crosses the negative real axis. Crossing \(-1\) would mean instability is imminent.
questions.figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 220" role="img" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12"><title>gain crossover</title><line x1="48" y1="42.7" x2="270" y2="42.7"/><polygon points="270,42.7 263.6,45.4 263.6,40" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"/><line x1="139.9" y1="180" x2="139.9" y2="28"/><polygon points="139.9,28 142.6,34.4 137.1,34.4" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"/><text x="266" y="56.7" text-anchor="end" font-size="11" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">Re</text><text x="145.9" y="32" text-anchor="start" font-size="11" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">Im</text><polyline points="254.7,42.7 201.1,116.3 139.9,165.3 101.6,140.8 86.3,42.7" stroke-width="2.2"/><circle cx="63.3" cy="42.7" r="4"/><text x="63.3" y="32.7" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">−1</text></svg>
questions.figure_alt: A curve in the complex plane with the critical point marked.
options: the curve crossing the unit circle centered at the origin
the curve crossing the real axis
the curve at its maximum imaginary part

questions.prompt: The Nyquist curve crosses the negative real axis at \(-0.5\). The gain margin is
questions.explanation: Gain margin is how much the loop gain can increase before the crossing reaches \(-1\). If the crossing is at \(-0.5\), the gain can double: \(GM = 1/0.5 = 2\). In dB, that is about 6 dB.
questions.figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 220" role="img" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12"><title>gain margin</title><line x1="48" y1="104" x2="270" y2="104"/><polygon points="270,104 263.6,106.7 263.6,101.3" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"/><line x1="127.1" y1="180" x2="127.1" y2="28"/><polygon points="127.1,28 129.8,34.4 124.4,34.4" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"/><text x="266" y="118" text-anchor="end" font-size="11" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">Re</text><text x="133.1" y="32" text-anchor="start" font-size="11" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">Im</text><polyline points="254.7,104 190.9,165.3 127.1,165.3 95.2,104 127.1,42.7 190.9,42.7 254.7,104" stroke-width="2.2"/><circle cx="63.3" cy="104" r="4"/><text x="63.3" y="94" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">−1</text></svg>
questions.figure_alt: A curve in the complex plane with the critical point marked.

questions.prompt: Same curve, crossing at \(-0.5\). The gain margin in dB is
questions.explanation: GM in dB is \(20 \log_{10}(2) = 6.02\) dB. The factor of 2 corresponds to about 6 dB. A crossing at \(-0.25\) would give 12 dB.
questions.figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 220" role="img" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12"><title>GM in dB</title><line x1="48" y1="104" x2="270" y2="104"/><polygon points="270,104 263.6,106.7 263.6,101.3" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"/><line x1="127.1" y1="180" x2="127.1" y2="28"/><polygon points="127.1,28 129.8,34.4 124.4,34.4" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"/><text x="266" y="118" text-anchor="end" font-size="11" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">Re</text><text x="133.1" y="32" text-anchor="start" font-size="11" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">Im</text><polyline points="254.7,104 190.9,165.3 127.1,165.3 95.2,104 127.1,42.7 190.9,42.7 254.7,104" stroke-width="2.2"/><circle cx="63.3" cy="104" r="4"/><text x="63.3" y="94" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">−1</text></svg>
questions.figure_alt: A curve in the complex plane with the critical point marked.

questions.explanation: Phase margin is how much additional phase lag can be added before instability. At \(|L| = 1\), the distance from \(-180°\) to the actual phase is the phase margin. Gain margin is measured at the phase crossover.
questions.figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 220" role="img" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12"><title>phase margin</title><line x1="48" y1="42.7" x2="270" y2="42.7"/><polygon points="270,42.7 263.6,45.4 263.6,40" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"/><line x1="159" y1="180" x2="159" y2="28"/><polygon points="159,28 161.7,34.4 156.3,34.4" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"/><text x="266" y="56.7" text-anchor="end" font-size="11" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">Re</text><text x="165" y="32" text-anchor="start" font-size="11" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">Im</text><polyline points="254.7,42.7 226,128.5 159,165.3" stroke-width="2.2"/><circle cx="63.3" cy="42.7" r="4"/><text x="63.3" y="32.7" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">−1</text></svg>
questions.figure_alt: A curve in the complex plane with the critical point marked.
options: the phase crossover frequency where the phase is \(-180°\)

questions.prompt: A loop has phase margin 45°. At the gain crossover, the phase of \(L(j\omega_c)\) is
questions.explanation: Phase margin is \(180° + \angle L\). If PM = 45°, then \(\angle L = -180° + 45° = -135°\). The phase at crossover is not \(-45°\); that would be 135° of margin.
questions.figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 220" role="img" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12"><title>phase at crossover</title><line x1="48" y1="42.7" x2="270" y2="42.7"/><polygon points="270,42.7 263.6,45.4 263.6,40" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"/><line x1="127.1" y1="180" x2="127.1" y2="28"/><polygon points="127.1,28 129.8,34.4 124.4,34.4" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"/><text x="266" y="56.7" text-anchor="end" font-size="11" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">Re</text><text x="133.1" y="32" text-anchor="start" font-size="11" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">Im</text><polyline points="254.7,42.7 190.9,124.4 127.1,165.3" stroke-width="2.2"/><circle cx="63.3" cy="42.7" r="4"/><text x="63.3" y="32.7" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">−1</text></svg>
questions.figure_alt: A curve in the complex plane with the critical point marked.

questions.prompt: For a stable open-loop with one clockwise encirclement of \(-1\), the closed-loop has
questions.explanation: Nyquist formula: \(Z = N + P\). With \(P = 0\) (stable open-loop) and \(N = 1\) (one clockwise encirclement), \(Z = 1\). The closed-loop has one unstable pole.
questions.figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 220" role="img" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12"><title>one encirclement</title><line x1="48" y1="104" x2="270" y2="104"/><polygon points="270,104 263.6,106.7 263.6,101.3" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"/><line x1="145.3" y1="180" x2="145.3" y2="28"/><polygon points="145.3,28 148.1,34.4 142.6,34.4" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"/><text x="266" y="118" text-anchor="end" font-size="11" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">Re</text><text x="151.3" y="32" text-anchor="start" font-size="11" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">Im</text><polyline points="254.7,104 145.3,165.3 63.3,119.3 90.7,104 63.3,88.7 145.3,42.7 254.7,104" stroke-width="2.2"/><circle cx="90.7" cy="104" r="4"/><text x="90.7" y="94" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">−1</text></svg>
questions.figure_alt: A curve in the complex plane with the critical point marked.
options: the same number of RHP poles as the open-loop

questions.prompt: A loop has gain margin 4 (factor) and the plant gain increases by a factor of 3. The new gain margin is
questions.explanation: The new loop gain is 3 times the old. The crossing point moves closer to \(-1\). The new margin is \(4/3 = 1.33\). The system is still stable but with less margin.
questions.figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 220" role="img" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12"><title>reduced margin</title><line x1="48" y1="42.7" x2="270" y2="42.7"/><polygon points="270,42.7 263.6,45.4 263.6,40" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"/><line x1="111.2" y1="180" x2="111.2" y2="28"/><polygon points="111.2,28 113.9,34.4 108.4,34.4" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"/><text x="266" y="56.7" text-anchor="end" font-size="11" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">Re</text><text x="117.2" y="32" text-anchor="start" font-size="11" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">Im</text><polyline points="254.7,42.7 182.9,165.3 75.3,42.7" stroke-width="2.2"/><circle cx="63.3" cy="42.7" r="4"/><text x="63.3" y="32.7" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">−1</text></svg>
questions.figure_alt: A curve in the complex plane with the critical point marked.

questions.prompt: For describing function analysis of a nonlinear system, the Nyquist plot is used to
questions.explanation: The describing function is the complex gain of a nonlinearity as a function of amplitude. Where the negative inverse intersects the Nyquist curve of the linear part, a limit cycle may occur. This extends Nyquist to nonlinear prediction.
questions.figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 220" role="img" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12"><title>describing function</title><line x1="48" y1="42.7" x2="270" y2="42.7"/><polygon points="270,42.7 263.6,45.4 263.6,40" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"/><line x1="159" y1="180" x2="159" y2="28"/><polygon points="159,28 161.7,34.4 156.3,34.4" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"/><text x="266" y="56.7" text-anchor="end" font-size="11" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">Re</text><text x="165" y="32" text-anchor="start" font-size="11" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">Im</text><polyline points="254.7,42.7 159,165.3 82.4,104 101.6,42.7" stroke-width="2.2"/><circle cx="63.3" cy="42.7" r="4"/><text x="63.3" y="32.7" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">−1</text></svg>
questions.figure_alt: A curve in the complex plane with the critical point marked.
options: find intersections that predict limit cycles

questions.prompt: The Nyquist curve's closest approach to \(-1\) is 0.4. The peak sensitivity \(M_s\) is
questions.explanation: Peak sensitivity is the reciprocal of the minimum distance to \(-1\): \(M_s = 1/0.4 = 2.5\). A smaller distance means larger sensitivity peak and less robust stability.
questions.figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 220" role="img" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12"><title>peak sensitivity</title><line x1="48" y1="42.7" x2="270" y2="42.7"/><polygon points="270,42.7 263.6,45.4 263.6,40" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"/><line x1="159" y1="180" x2="159" y2="28"/><polygon points="159,28 161.7,34.4 156.3,34.4" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"/><text x="266" y="56.7" text-anchor="end" font-size="11" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">Re</text><text x="165" y="32" text-anchor="start" font-size="11" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">Im</text><polyline points="254.7,42.7 159,165.3 101.6,79.5 111.2,42.7" stroke-width="2.2"/><circle cx="63.3" cy="42.7" r="4"/><text x="63.3" y="32.7" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">−1</text></svg>

questions.prompt: An open-loop unstable system with two RHP poles needs the Nyquist curve to
questions.explanation: For \(Z = 0\) closed-loop RHP poles, we need \(N = -P = -2\). Two counter-clockwise encirclements (negative in the convention) cancel the two open-loop RHP poles. Clockwise encirclements would add unstable poles.
